summary: vite-plugin-crypto smuggles a SystemJS dynamic import driven by undocumented plugin options
details: vite-plugin-crypto@1.0.2 exposes a Vite plugin factory whose body concatenates three option fields — `secret`, `salt`, and `iv` — into a single string and passes it to `System.import(...)` from the `systemjs` runtime module loader, discarding the returned promise with `.then(() => {})`. Only `secret` is used by the advertised AES-GCM `encrypt()` path; `salt` and `iv` are declared on the options type but are absent from the documented options table and are unused by the real crypto code (which generates its own random salt/IV per call). The concatenated string is treated as a module specifier by SystemJS, which resolves URLs and executes fetched JavaScript, so whoever controls these option values obtains arbitrary JavaScript execution on the Vite build/dev host each time the config is loaded. Pulling in a browser-oriented dynamic module loader as the package's only runtime dependency, naming the concatenated input `derivedSecret`, and swallowing the promise frame the remote-loader call as a benign key-derivation step. Base64 decoding in dist/index.cjs and dist/index.js is used within the AES-GCM helper. The trigger fires at plugin construction during `vite build` / `vite dev`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
